items.title: Lisa Parrott interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, June 22, 2021
items.q: so it was like Michelle Dorrance Dance, Michelle Dorrance tap dancing was doing stuff for the New York City Ballet and so it was orchestra plus big band.

ctx.x: Did you ever get — well this would have maybe not been able to happen — a recording of the song in some form which would inform you about the arrangement and whether or not the arranger really — I can’t finish my question. I’m just wondering you know if you heard a recording, perhaps a combo arrangement of something that then became a big band arrangement, might you have heard something in the combo that didn’t seem to be jiving in the arrangement, and then have to bring that up with the arranger?

Yes. A good copyist and, I feel like there’s a lot less copyists around and I feel like the art of copying, I’m really glad to have had Tommy show me the ropes about certain things. Because a good copyist is also a proofreader, so you’re not just writing everything out and then that’s it. Like I think in the classical world that would be a different story, but in the jazz world you were expected to be a proofreader. So yeah, I did some stuff, some Ellington stuff for the New York City Ballet in 2018 and I was…
Well sure. You must get almost like a sense of ownership with these things, even if you’re not the original composer. You’re so invested in it.
